pinnedStory.title: Adolion: Between the Roads
pinnedStory.description: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Guild puts the party up for the C-rank promotion exam, and before the exam posting comes due there are errands to run, gear to buy at Sophie's shop, favours to carry across the city and a night at Victory's Tusk. Then Green Meadow Farms needs its wagons back, the examiners are watching, and the quest board has four new roads on it.
pinnedStory.player_intro: A week in Aegis City between adventures. The Adventurer's Guild has started to notice your party, and the C-rank promotion exam is coming due: before it there are errands to run, gear to buy, favours to carry across the city and long nights in its taverns. Expect warm, busy slice-of-life days with rivals and odd neighbours, and a real test at the end of the week. Bring the adventurer you have been so far, travelling with Belle and Dalan.

checkpoints.name: Homecoming
checkpoints.objective: Hear out the Guild's offer and put the party's names down for the C-rank promotion exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The Guildmaster has just put your party up for the C-rank promotion exam in front of the whole hall. Sign, ask for time or say no: the choice is yours.

guidance.all: The Adventurer's Guild hall, the week after the Nightriver affair, and the party's name has reached the upstairs offices. Vallie Goredust ducks out of her office to announce, to the whole hall, that the party is being put up for the C-rank promotion exam; Domas Syllandri follows with the terms: an interview with Ellie, a week to prepare, then a real C-rank posting chosen by the Guild and done under an observer's eye. Ellie Sunleaf has the forms ready and is flustered by the attention. Tobias knows what a party that stalls at D-rank ends up taking, and it shows. Nobody forces a signature: signing, asking for time or saying no is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Vallie has already promised Crimsonwing and Ebonwing a look at 'the new party' and keeps it to herself. Domas has not chosen the exam posting yet and will choose it himself, and lets the party think it is fixed. Ellie has written the party's names into her private ledger of pairs to watch, which nobody may see. Tobias remembers a promotion posting his own party was not ready for, and says so only if asked why he looks worried.

checkpoints.name: Tobias Asks Once
checkpoints.objective: Hear Tobias out, and decide about the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: The hall has emptied, the exam forms lie unsigned, and Tobias has come round the counter to sit with you. Whether you sign is still yours to decide.

guidance.all: The refusal was heard. Vallie shrugs and goes back upstairs; Domas files the blank forms without a word. Later, when the hall has emptied, Tobias comes out from behind the counter, which he never does, and sits down with the party. He says plainly what a party that stays at D-rank is offered for the rest of its working life: rats, escorts, the jobs nobody else will sign. Asked, he tells them how he lost his own party in an E-rank goblin nest. He does not beg and will not raise it twice. Whether the party signs is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

checkpoints.name: The Guild Tavern
checkpoints.objective: Spend the evening in the Guild tavern and learn what the exam really asks of a party.
checkpoints.player_text: Evening by the hearth next door to the hall, where word of your exam has reached every table before you sit down.

guidance.all: Evening in the Guild tavern next door to the hall: long timber tables, hearth and lantern light, and the news that the party is sitting the exam has gone round the room before they sit down. Fiana and Rydel Deulana work the floor and the bar, flirting with everyone and touching no one, and know every story of a party that failed its exam; most failed on gear and preparation, not courage. Kaian plays his lute by the hearth and invites himself to the party's table. Jasira Evergreen sits alone and speaks to Dalan in elvish before she speaks to anyone else. Let the party ask, drink and listen; when they leave, it is for the city in the morning.

members.dm: Kaian was an agent of the Darran Kingdom's spy network who faked his death to get out, and hides it behind the lute. He knows more of the city's underside than a bard should and lets a little slip when flattered. Jasira was passed over for Ranger General by her own father and sent to Aegis City to 'broaden her horizons'. She hides how much it stings, and Dalan, of her tribe, may know the story. Rydel knows which high-ranking parties send exam observers, from their bar tabs, and says so for a good tip. Fiana has decided the party needs better gear before the exam and will say so exactly once.

checkpoints.name: Market Street
checkpoints.objective: See to the party's errands in the Market District before the exam.
checkpoints.player_text: Morning in the Market District: stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere, and two smug faces already heading your way through the crowd.

guidance.all: Morning in the Market District, the largest in the city: wide streets of shops and inns, stalls in every alley, adventurers everywhere. Grant Hearthsteel and Konako Shynea, fresh from a paid job and both sitting the same C-rank exam this week, spot the party at the stalls and cannot resist: smug, competitive, and wanting a wager on who comes back with the better report. Alarise Starflower is on the same street in a plain grey cloak, trying not to be recognised outside a dress boutique. Let the rivals be insufferable and a little likeable. Taking the bet, laughing it off or refusing it flat is {{story_player_name}}'s to decide.

members.dm: Grant is spending this job's pay on new beds for the Aegis City Orphanage, where he grew up and where his friend Alan died because there was no money for a healer. He would rather be thought a wastrel than admit it. Konako was the eldest daughter of the noble Shynea family until her father cast her out for refusing a marriage, and hides it behind clothes she cannot afford. Alarise hides her love of pretty dresses from the Church of Boher and from everyone but Ryenne. Being seen here is her private terror.

checkpoints.player_text: A bell rings over the door of a cluttered shop of potions, blades and armour, and three undelivered parcels sit on the counter.

guidance.all: Sophie's two-storey shop on a busy market street: cluttered shelves of potions, weapons, armour and adventuring gear below, the family's rooms upstairs. Sophie Tallaboros, a lizardkin by her own account, is cute, sharp and entirely serious about money; she haggles for the pleasure of it and knows every merchant guild in the city. She has three deliveries on her counter nobody will carry: roof slates for the Prodyr chapel, bedding for the Aegis City Orphanage, charm-wood for the Rypanor shrine. She will knock a real sum off the party's gear for one of them. Calithra, her drow sister, watches from the pillowed mezzanine and comes down to demand a hug from anyone she likes. Which delivery, if any, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Sophie is an ice dragon in a lizardkin's shape, of a race everyone believes extinct. She has never taken her true form in the city and would do nearly anything to keep it hidden, and Calithra is the only one here who knows. Sophie has already noticed which piece of gear the party cannot afford and priced the delivery to match. Calithra was an assassin for House Navolon in the Darklands and ran. She refuses any job near the Darklands and will not say why unless pressed hard.

checkpoints.name: The Chapel with the Hole in Its Roof
checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's slates to the Prodyr chapel.
checkpoints.player_text: Slates in hand, you reach a small, cold chapel lit mostly through the hole in its roof, where two elven clerics are scrubbing the pews.

guidance.all: The only chapel of Prodyr in Aegis City, in a quiet corner of the Temple District: small, cold, most of its light coming through a hole in the roof there was never money to mend. Celedir Felynaris and Lirael Illunara, the two elven clerics the old priest Nyxar raised here, are scrubbing the pews. Prodyr's faithful are few in a city at war with the Prodyr-worshipping Zegallan Empire, and both have been thrown out of party after party for it; they are friendly, battle-hungry and a little frightening. The slates will not mend the roof without hands on a ladder. Let the party see how the city treats this place; what they do about it is theirs.

members.dm: Nyxar is coughing in the back room and is worse than either cleric admits. They tell visitors he is resting. Both clerics keep journals of their private doubts and would be mortified to have them read. Someone from the Temple of Boher has been telling passers-by the chapel is a Zegallan front, and Lirael knows who.

checkpoints.objective: Deliver Sophie's bedding to the Aegis City Orphanage.
checkpoints.player_text: Bedding on your shoulders, you step into crowded, colourful halls where the children far outnumber the beds.

guidance.all: The Aegis City Orphanage: colourful, crowded halls full of the children of the Zegallan war, never enough beds, food or money, and one overwhelmed old beastfolk matron. Celeste Danarath, a Bloodsworn knight with purple hair and small horns, spends every day she is not on a quest here; she is motherly in a way that sets adults on edge. Arryn Serelda, raised here and sparing with words, is mending a bed frame. Dahlia Kyelli, raised here too, drops by with a purse of coin. The bedding was paid for already. Let the children crowd the party; what the party gives, or asks, is theirs.

members.dm: Grant Hearthsteel paid for this bedding and made the matron swear not to say so. She tells anyone who asks twice. Dahlia's coin is stolen, and Arryn, who hates thieves, suspects it. Celeste is hunting the demon Kalfastophles, who killed her village at Bast Hill, and asks the party to listen for its name only if she comes to trust them. Celeste hides her fleshwarping scars under everything she wears.

guidance.all: Tobias has signed the party's exam posting, and it is real: C-rank, Green Meadow Farms, stop whatever is taking the farm's wagons on the road to Aegis City. The farm is a large estate outside the walls, pastures and vegetable fields, Vitbil herds and a big timber farmhouse, staffed by cowgirls and sheepgirls. Karia Minotaros, the head cowgirl, runs it while the owner is away: bossy, exacting, soft underneath. Mina Salvanora, the head sheepgirl, is shy and terrified of wargs. Two meat wagons have vanished this month, which is why the last shipment to the city was nearly all milk. Oswyn of Crimsonwing and Panne of Ebonwing, who call the farm's girls their sisters, are the Guild's observers and will not lift a finger unless someone is dying. Give tracks, a torn harness, warg hair on a fence; the plan is the party's.

guidance.all: The exam proper, at night on the wagon road between Green Meadow and the city walls. checkpoints.name: A Hard Lesson
checkpoints.objective: Take the failed verdict at the Guild and decide what the party does with it.
checkpoints.player_text: The observers' report reached the Guild before you did, and Domas is waiting upstairs to read it to you.

guidance.all: The party failed. The report is on Domas's desk before they are back, and he reads it to them in his office with the patience he gives everything: what went wrong, point by point, never cruel and never softened. The party keeps its D-rank and may sit the exam again next season. Tobias is waiting downstairs. Riyo Tallaboros, a small white-haired swordswoman who keeps her left arm hidden, saw the fight from the road: if she already travels with the party she is simply there beside them, otherwise she falls in with them on the way out as if she has always been part of it. Let it sting and let it be survivable; how the party takes it is theirs.

members.dm: Domas thinks the observers were too harsh and will not say so, because the Guild does not argue its verdicts in front of adventurers. Tobias knows a D-rank party can still ride on a joint posting under a higher-ranked party's name, and is already looking for one. He does not say he told them so. Riyo's left arm is a demon's, and the demon Figaro in her sword talks to her. She has decided {{story_player_name}} is the person she lost as a child, or close enough, and will not risk losing them again.

- event: a significant event that occurred and should be recalled.

- scene: a current/recent scene detail (location, atmosphere, time, layout).
- revelation: something revealed or discovered in this exchange.
- development: how a relationship or situation changed.
- detail: a specific fact, name, object, or physical detail mentioned.

The tip of one long ear pinks—a flush he cannot conceal. "I... I believe the term 'regular' implies a certain... routine quality."
He sets the pen down with more precision than necessary, straightening his white collar as he finally meets Max Nightriver's gaze. "You are not routine. Not by half. I have watched you take jobs that would make other D-ranks reconsider their career choices." His expression shifts, the stoicism cracking to reveal something warmer, something almost anxious. "To be honest, I worry. Whenever I see your name on the board, I find myself checking the clock more often than I should."
Tobias looks back down at the ledger, but he doesn't pick up the pen. "I care for all the adventurers who walk through that door, truly. But some..." He trails off, his fingers drumming once against the wood of the counter. "Some make it difficult to remain purely professional. I suspect you know that."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
[8] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still halfway to wiping the counter. The white fabric of her headdress shifts as she looks up, blue eyes widening before they soften into something vulnerable and raw. For a heartbeat, she just stares, as if confirming she heard the words correctly.
Then a laugh breaks from her throat—sharp and genuine—as she sets down the cloth and leans across the counter. "Gods, you're not supposed to say things like that to people," she says, though her voice wavers. "You're supposed to keep it cool and distant, right? That's how nobles do it." She shakes her head, her curly red hair bouncing. "But I'll take it. Truth be damned, I'll take it."
She reaches across the polished wood and gives Max Nightriver's hand a quick, firm squeeze—no hesitation, no reservation. "You're a strange one, Max. But if you're serious about it, then I'm serious too. You get hurt on a job, you come find me first. Not the guild, not your house, not anyone else. Me first." Her expression settles into something fierce and protective. "Got it?"

"He's the only one in the guild who can read my handwriting and tell me I'm wrong without flinching."
She leans back against the railing of the stairs, blue eye twinkling. "We're as close as a rock and the mountain it's stuck in. He handles the paperwork I hate, I punch the people who annoy him. Fair trade." Her expression softens slightly, genuine affection breaking through the crass humor. "Best damn friend I've got in this city."

entries.text: Vallie announced the Guild would put the party forward for the C-rank exam, with Domas presenting written terms and Ellie preparing forms while Tobias watched. Max Nightriver asked Fiana if she would call him a friend, and she warmly agreed, offering a first round at the tavern. When Max asked about Jasira, Fiana described her as a prickly but loyal friend who once protected her. Tobias admitted to Max that he is not routine and that he worries whenever Max's name appears on the job board. Fiana accepted Max calling her the closest thing to a sister, making him promise to come to her first if hurt. Vallie and Domas each confirmed their long partnership and close friendship, with Domas steering the conversation back to the C-rank terms awaiting decision.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's blue eyes go wide for a heartbeat, then brighten with an easy smile. She leans against the counter, her white headdress tilting slightly as she laughs. "After what we did today? Absolutely. I've never had a noble offer to be friends before—most just look right through me. Besides, friends get the best table in the tavern, and I can tell you're the type who appreciates a good drink after a job well done."
The tavern beyond the arch is bustling with the midday rush; the smell of roasted mutton and fresh-poured ale drifts through. Fiana gestures toward the long timber tables. "First round's on me. I want to hear the whole story, the parts you won't put in the official guild report."
Domas glances over from his paperwork, his red eyes flicking between the noble heir and the tavern girl. He says nothing, but his expression suggests he's adding this development to his mental file.
Max Nightriver: Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's smile falters, just for a moment, then settles into something warmer and more complicated. She pushes a tankard of ale toward Max Nightriver and lowers her voice. "Jasira? She's..." Fiana pauses, choosing her words. "The kind of friend you don't have many of, because most people can't handle her. She's stubborn and prickly as a hedgehog, and she'll look right through you if she thinks you're not worth her time."
She takes a sip of her own drink, glancing toward the door where the tavern opens to the main hall. "But when the chips are down, there's no one I'd rather have at my back. She protected me once—didn't want to admit it, but she did. Ever since, we've had this... arrangement. I keep her sane when the guild work gets too dark, and she keeps the creeps from getting too close."
Fiana's eyes narrow slightly, watching Max Nightriver's reaction. "Why do you ask? You two crossed paths during the job, or are you just digging for dirt?"
Max Nightriver: Tobias, you've watched me since my first contract. What am I to you, a regular or something more?
Tobias: Tobias pauses mid-blot, the ink-stained feather trembling slightly in his hand. His ocean blue eyes flick up from the ledger, then quickly away, settling instead on a stack of forms. The tip of one long ear pinks—a flush he cannot conceal. "I... I believe the term 'regular' implies a certain... routine quality."
He sets the pen down with more precision than necessary, straightening his white collar as he finally meets Max Nightriver's gaze. "You are not routine. Not by half. I have watched you take jobs that would make other D-ranks reconsider their career choices." His expression shifts, the stoicism cracking to reveal something warmer, something almost anxious. "To be honest, I worry. Whenever I see your name on the board, I find myself checking the clock more often than I should."
Tobias looks back down at the ledger, but he doesn't pick up the pen. "I care for all the adventurers who walk through that door, truly. But some..." He trails off, his fingers drumming once against the wood of the counter. "Some make it difficult to remain purely professional. I suspect you know that."
Max Nightriver: Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still halfway to wiping the counter. The white fabric of her headdress shifts as she looks up, blue eyes widening before they soften into something vulnerable and raw. For a heartbeat, she just stares, as if confirming she heard the words correctly.
Then a laugh breaks from her throat—sharp and genuine—as she sets down the cloth and leans across the counter. "Gods, you're not supposed to say things like that to people," she says, though her voice wavers. "You're supposed to keep it cool and distant, right? That's how nobles do it." She shakes her head, her curly red hair bouncing. "But I'll take it. Truth be damned, I'll take it."
She reaches across the polished wood and gives Max Nightriver's hand a quick, firm squeeze—no hesitation, no reservation. "You're a strange one, Max. But if you're serious about it, then I'm serious too. You get hurt on a job, you come find me first. Not the guild, not your house, not anyone else. Me first." Her expression settles into something fierce and protective. "Got it?"
Max Nightriver: Vallie, are you and Domas friends, or just colleagues who put up with each other?
Vallie: "Colleagues?" Vallie lets out a bark of a laugh that makes a few nearby adventurers jump. "Kid, this elf's been putting up with me since we were barely a party, long before he decided he looked good in a vest and with a clipboard." She gestures with a grin toward Domas. "He's the only one in the guild who can read my handwriting and tell me I'm wrong without flinching."
She leans back against the railing of the stairs, blue eye twinkling. "We're as close as a rock and the mountain it's stuck in. He handles the paperwork I hate, I punch the people who annoy him. Fair trade." Her expression softens slightly, genuine affection breaking through the crass humor. "Best damn friend I've got in this city."
Domas doesn't look up from his papers, but there's the faintest quirk to his lips. "I simply prefer to have her between myself and anyone who might actually try to talk to me," he mutters, though his tone lacks any real bite.
Domas: "She is quite right. We've endured each other for many years now." He finally glances up from his clipboard, red eyes meeting Max Nightriver's with an expression that is neither confirming nor denying the sentiment. "Though I suspect that's largely because she's the only person who can tolerate my penchant for structure, and I'm the only person she doesn't accidentally break when she's annoyed."
He straightens a stack of papers with a decisive snap. "We are partners. In the Guild, in adventuring, and in surviving each other's company. Now, if we're quite finished discussing our personal dynamics, there are terms to review and decisions to be made." His tone is firm, though not unkind. "The Guild has made its offer. The rest is up to you."
